Quantify gene activity from indexed ATAC fragments

Source: R/RunGeneActivity.R
RunGeneActivity.Rd

Run native Signac::GeneActivity() with explicit annotation and counting parameters, then store the sparse result in a new gene-activity assay. Activity measures accessibility over gene bodies and promoters; it is not measured RNA expression and does not establish regulatory links.

Usage

RunGeneActivity(
  object,
  assay = NULL,
  new.assay = "ACTIVITY",
  features = NULL,
  extend.upstream = 2000,
  extend.downstream = 0,
  biotypes = "protein_coding",
  max.width = 5e+05,
  process_n = 2000,
  gene.id = FALSE,
  normalize = TRUE,
  scale.factor = 10000,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

object

A Seurat object with a validated ChromatinAssay.

assay

Source chromatin assay; defaults to the active assay.

new.assay

An unused assay name. Existing assays are never overwritten.

features, extend.upstream, extend.downstream, biotypes, max.width, process_n, gene.id

Parameters passed unchanged to Signac::GeneActivity().

normalize

Whether to populate the new assay's data layer using native Seurat LogNormalize. Raw activity counts remain in counts.

scale.factor

LogNormalize scale factor, used only when normalizing.

verbose

Whether native backends print progress messages.

Value

The Seurat object with a new activity assay and a source receipt in Misc(object[[new.assay]], "scop_gene_activity"). The default assay, source counts, original metadata columns and existing reductions are unchanged. Native count-QC columns may be added for the new assay. The receipt records active fragment resources and calculation-time IDs; later native subsetting or renaming does not synchronize this snapshot. Caller RNG state is restored.

Details

Attach a verified transcript annotation with Signac::Annotation() before calling this function. Its reference label must equal the source assay's label. Required fields are gene_id, gene_name and gene_biotype; gene_id must be non-missing and non-empty on every row. Repeated gene IDs may describe multiple transcripts only on the same contig and native strand (unstranded rows are treated as plus strand). Native Signac collapses transcript coordinates to gene spans, extends promoter intervals, and counts fragment-record overlaps; this wrapper does not substitute peak sums. Native handling of missing chromosomes and gene filtering is retained. Output genes and all source-assay cells are recorded in the assay receipt. Native Signac disambiguates repeated gene symbols; use gene.id = TRUE for stable gene identifiers. Final output IDs must be unique and survive native Seurat assay creation unchanged. Native backends that drop matrix dimensions for a single retained gene or cell are rejected rather than reconstructed. Width filtering uses the gene span before promoter extension; native gene filtering and missing-contig behavior do not establish sequencing coverage.

Duplicate native output IDs, including distinct genes sharing an identical counting window, are rejected explicitly. No private version-specific recovery, synthetic IDs, row summation or silent gene dropping is performed. Select unambiguous genes or revise the annotation explicitly before retrying. Gene IDs alone do not resolve identical counting windows; their counts cannot distinguish the associated genes.

See also

ReadATACData(), CheckATACData()

Examples

if (requireNamespace("Rsamtools", quietly = TRUE)) {
  (function() {
    directory <- tempfile("activity_example_")
    dir.create(directory)
    on.exit(unlink(directory, recursive = TRUE))
    plain <- file.path(directory, "fragments.tsv")
    writeLines(c(
      "chr1\t100\t120\tA\t5", "chr1\t300\t320\tB\t2",
      "chr1\t610\t630\tC\t3"
    ), plain)
    path <- paste0(plain, ".gz")
    Rsamtools::bgzip(plain, dest = path, overwrite = TRUE)
    Rsamtools::indexTabix(path, format = "bed")
    ranges <- GenomicRanges::makeGRangesFromDataFrame(data.frame(
      seqnames = "chr1", start = c(101, 301, 601), end = c(150, 350, 650)
    ))
    annotation <- ranges
    GenomeInfoDb::genome(annotation) <- "toy"
    annotation$gene_id <- paste0("GENE", 1:3)
    annotation$gene_name <- annotation$gene_id
    annotation$gene_biotype <- "protein_coding"
    annotation$type <- "gene"
    annotation$tx_id <- annotation$gene_id
    counts <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(
      i = 1:3, j = 1:3, x = 1,
      dimnames = list(paste0("p", 1:3), c("A", "B", "C"))
    )
    atac <- ReadATACData(counts,
      ranges = ranges, genome = "toy", annotation = annotation,
      fragments = path, fragment.cells = c(A = "A", B = "B", C = "C"), verbose = FALSE
    )
    activity <- RunGeneActivity(atac, gene.id = TRUE, extend.upstream = 0, verbose = FALSE)
    SeuratObject::GetAssayData(activity, assay = "ACTIVITY", layer = "counts")
  })()
}
#> 3 x 3 sparse Matrix of class "dgCMatrix"
#>       A B C
#> GENE1 1 . .
#> GENE2 . 1 .
#> GENE3 . . 1
